08-lang-wrong.html.note: Page declares lang=en over Spanish content. SPEC 5 defers the rule until this fixture shows how it fails. The language assertion is skipped here on purpose; the axe assertion still applies.

10-icon-only-controls.html.note: No vision tier applies to a link or a button. Every name here must come from href, svg markup or a nested <title> — free, no model. tier 'none' is a failure, not an honest floor.

15-banner-above-field.html.note: The field's own placeholder must beat a promotional banner several levels above it. Text authored for a region is not a label for a field inside it.

14-class-only-controls.html.note: Captured from elcomercio.pe: carousel buttons whose icons are CSS backgrounds. No SVG, no text, no title — the class name is the only word the author wrote.

11-duplicate-ids.html.note: Two inputs share one id. Each must get its OWN label from its own context — the second is a phone field and must not inherit the first's email label. Checked by position, since the ids cannot tell them apart.

real/minsa-noticias/index.html.note: SPEC §6 criterion 5. Captured 2026-09-04 from gob.pe/institucion/minsa/noticias — the DOM the browser built, not the HTML the server sent, because the gaps on a modern site live in what JavaScript injected. Stylesheets are downloaded rather than dropped: deleting them un-hides whatever the page hides with CSS, and a snapshot that alters visibility measures a page nobody visits. Verified identical to live (label:2) and fully offline.

13-loop-provocation.html.note: Zero axe violations on purpose: an with a title has an accessible name, so image-alt does not fire. The name is in the wrong language, which only criterion 2 can see — the pair earning its keep again. SPEC §6 criterion 3. The English title makes T1 answer in English on a Spanish page; the verifier rejects for language and the reason escalates as feedback. Deterministic on the rejection; the pass needs a profile with the on-device model.
